item.title: Canada announces counter-tariffs on over 700 U.S. goods
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
Wood logs are pictured floating in the Fraser River in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada, Aug. 25, 2026. The Canadian federal government on Tuesday announced retaliatory tariffs on over 700 U.S. goods valued at 27.6 billion Canadian dollars (about 20 billion U.S. dollars), alongside a 7.5-billion-Canadian-dollar assistance package for domestic businesses and workers. (Photo by Liang Sen/Xinhua)
OTTAWA, Aug. 25 (Xinhua) -- The Canadian federal government on Tuesday announced retaliatory tariffs on over 700 U.S. goods valued at 27.6 billion Canadian dollars (about 20 billion U.S. dollars), alongside a 7.5-billion-Canadian-dollar assistance package for domestic businesses and workers.
Canadian officials said the countermeasures match the total value of Canadian products targeted by the latest 50-percent U.S. tariffs, achieving a "dollar-for-dollar, rate for rate" response. The counter-tariffs are scheduled to take effect officially on Sept. 8.
Canadian Finance Minister Francois-Philippe Champagne said the reciprocal tariffs as well as the multi-billion-dollar support package will protect workers, farmers, families and businesses.
According to a list released by the Finance Ministry, the new targeted counter-tariffs are concentrated in sectors such as steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, and electronics, with tariff rates set at three tiers: 15 percent, 25 percent and 50 percent.
In certain sectors, such as steel and aluminum, existing counter-tariffs will increase from 25 percent to 50 percent to match U.S. rates. Other existing counter-tariffs, including those against U.S. autos, will also continue to apply, said the ministry.
A 25-percent tariff will be levied on dairy products such as cheese, fish, seafood, and certain steel and aluminum derivatives.
In addition to the tariffs, the federal government announced a 7.5-billion-Canadian-dollar relief package, primarily targeting small and medium-sized enterprises. Ottawa promised to help companies avoid layoffs, enable more workers to upgrade skills, and increase flexibility for accessing employment insurance.

item.title: China, US hold third Track 1.5 Dialogue in Beijing
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
The third China-US Track 1.5 Dialogue is held in Beijing, China, August 25, 2026. /IDCPC
China and the United States held the third Track 1.5 Dialogue in Beijing on Tuesday. The two sides engaged in candid, in-depth and constructive exchanges, and underscored that the China-US relationship is of vital importance and is currently at a critical juncture.
Both sides expressed the need to jointly implement the important common understandings reached by the two heads of state, build on the new positioning of the China-US constructive relationship of strategic stability, strengthen communication and dialogue, and enhance mutual political trust.
Representatives also called for promoting exchanges and cooperation in such areas as economy and trade, people-to-people and cultural ties, subnational cooperation, healthcare, artificial intelligence and food security, to properly handle differences and jointly address global challenges.
The dialogue was co-hosted by the International Department of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and the Asia Society of the United States. Liu Haixing, head of the International Department of the CPC Central Committee, attended the event and delivered a keynote speech.
Approximately 40 Chinese and US representatives participated in the dialogue, including personnel from relevant Chinese government departments, local governments, think tanks and universities, as well as US strategic and business community figures like John L. Thornton, co-chair of the Board of Trustees of the Asia Society.

item.title: Finland, Saudi Arabia guest countries of honor at 26th China int'l investment, trade fair
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
The State Council Information Office (SCIO) holds a press conference on the 26th China International Fair for Investment and Trade in Beijing, capital of China, Aug. 25, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Xulun)
BEIJING, Aug. 25 (Xinhua) -- The 26th China International Fair for Investment and Trade is set to take place from Sept. 8 to 11 in Xiamen, Fujian Province, with preparations now largely complete, Vice Commerce Minister Ling Ji said on Tuesday.
This year's edition introduces a "dual guest countries of honor" mechanism for the first time, with Finland and Saudi Arabia jointly assuming the role, Ling told a press conference.
"This underscores the fair's growing international appeal and its distinctive role in facilitating two-way investment," he said.
China is Finland's largest trading partner in Asia and its fourth largest globally. Last year, bilateral trade exceeded 8 billion U.S. dollars.
China is Saudi Arabia's largest trading partner, with bilateral trade exceeding 100 billion U.S. dollars for four consecutive years.
To date, delegations from 123 countries and regions have registered to participate in the upcoming fair, while 60 countries and regions will set up exhibition pavilions. Multinational companies and foreign business councils have registered in large numbers, Ling noted.
The fair will be structured around three core thematic sections: "Invest in China," "China's Outbound Investment" and "International Investment."
The event will feature 14 specialized exhibition zones, showcasing investment opportunities in new quality productive forces, the "Silk Road Maritime" initiative, international supply chains, and other promising sectors.

item.title: China mulls road safety law revisions, law against cross-border corruption
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
Zhao Leji, chairman of the National People's Congress (NPC) Standing Committee, presides over the first plenary meeting of the 24th session of the 14th NPC Standing Committee at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Aug. 25, 2026. (Xinhua/Pang Xinglei)
BEIJING, Aug. 25 (Xinhua) -- Chinese lawmakers convened on Tuesday to review a raft of bills, including draft revisions to the Road Traffic Safety Law, a draft law on combating cross-border corruption and a draft healthcare security law.
The bills were submitted for deliberation at the 24th session of the Standing Committee of the 14th National People's Congress (NPC), the country's top legislature.
Zhao Leji, chairman of the NPC Standing Committee, presided over the first plenary meeting of the session.
In the meeting, lawmakers deliberated a draft healthcare security law. Submitted for a third reading, the draft includes provisions on long-term care insurance, aiming to further protect the rights and interests of insured people.
A draft law on farmland protection and quality improvement was submitted for its third reading, adding provisions on talent cultivation and strengthening oversight of funds for high-standard farmland development.
Lawmakers also reviewed a revised draft of the Agriculture Law, which improves support for agricultural and rural economic development, enhances protection for farmers' rights and interests, and strengthens rural development and governance.
A draft revision to the National Defense Mobilization Law was submitted for its second reading. The revisions clarify the concept of national defense mobilization and rules on the collection, use and security management of relevant data.
Lawmakers reviewed a draft amendment to the lawyers law that improves the provisions to boost foreign-related legal services.
A revised draft of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, submitted for its second reading, refines rules on the bankruptcy of individual debtors bearing joint and several liability, improves the reorganization system, and adjusts the priority order for distributions from the bankruptcy estate.
Also under review was a revised draft of the banking supervision and regulation law, which introduces classified and tiered supervision of banking institutions, improves the system for protecting banking consumers' rights and interests, and adds a separate chapter on risk resolution.
Lawmakers also reviewed a revised draft of the Water Law. The second-reading draft strengthens provisions on the protection of water resources and water ecology, national water network development, and water conservation and recycling.
Draft revisions to the Road Traffic Safety Law were submitted for review, seeking to improve the road traffic safety management system and strengthen the legal framework for maintaining traffic order. The draft includes a dedicated chapter on autonomous vehicles.
A draft law on combating cross-border corruption was submitted for the first reading, aiming to prevent and punish transnational corruption, deepen international cooperation and safeguard national sovereignty, security, and development interests.
Lawmakers also heard a series of reports, including a report on the implementation of the 2026 plan for national economic and social development, a report on budget execution, a report on government debt management in 2025, and a supervisory research report on government debt management in 2025.
A report on improving the quality of cultural products and services and a report on efforts to consolidate and expand achievements in poverty alleviation and advance all-around rural revitalization were also on the agenda of the lawmakers.
Lawmakers also deliberated an extradition treaty between China and Hungary, a deputy qualification report and personnel-related bills.

item.title: Xi puts forward four principles on Palestinian question
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-25
Chinese President Xi Jinping holds talks with King of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan Abdullah II ibn Al Hussein, who is on a state visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Aug. 24, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Xiang)
BEIJING, Aug. 24 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping stressed on Monday that four principles should be followed to push for the resolution of the Palestinian question, which is at the heart of the Middle East issue.
Xi made the remarks in talks with King of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan Abdullah II ibn Al Hussein in Beijing.
First, a political settlement should be upheld. The two-state solution is the right direction, and efforts should be made to restart peace talks between Palestine and Israel, with a view to establishing an independent Palestinian state at an early date, Xi said.
Second, the principle of "Palestinians governing Palestine" should be followed in advancing the governance of the West Bank and the post-war reconstruction of Gaza, he said.
Third, humanitarian principles must be upheld. The international community, and the UN Security Council in particular, should shoulder its responsibility effectively to protect civilian safety, ensure the flow of humanitarian assistance, and put an end to humanitarian disasters, Xi said.
Fourth, fairness and justice must be upheld. This means following international law, addressing both symptoms and root causes, and taking practical actions so that the Palestinian question can be resolved in a comprehensive, just and lasting way at an early date, he said.
On the Middle East situation, Xi said China has always advocated a comprehensive ceasefire and end of hostilities, and resolving disputes through political and diplomatic means, adding that the sovereignty and security of Jordan and all other countries in the region should be respected.
Noting Jordan appreciates China's impartial stance on Middle East affairs and its support for the just cause of Arab countries, King Abdullah II said Jordan is ready to maintain close communication with China and continue to make active efforts for de-escalation.

item.title: Xi congratulates Alamgir on assuming Bangladeshi presidency
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-25
BEIJING, Aug. 24 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Monday extended congratulations to Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on assuming the office as president of Bangladesh.
In his congratulatory message, Xi noted China and Bangladesh are traditional friendly neighbors.
Xi said that since the establishment of diplomatic ties 51 years ago, the two countries have enjoyed mutual respect, treated each other as equals, supported each other on issues of their respective core interests and major concerns, and joined hands on their paths towards modernization.
Bilateral relations have withstood the tests of a rapidly changing international situation, Xi said.
Xi said he attaches great importance to the development of China-Bangladesh relations, and is willing to work with Alamgir to carry forward the traditional friendship, strengthen strategic communication, advance high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, deepen exchanges and cooperation in all fields, and guide the building of a China-Bangladesh community with a shared future in the new era to go deeper and more solid, so as to better benefit the two peoples.

item.title: Xi stresses consolidating, expanding campaign on correct view of governance performance
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-25
BEIJING, Aug. 24 (Xinhua) -- Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, has emphasized the importance of consolidating and expanding the progress made in a Party-wide study and education campaign for establishing and practicing a correct understanding of governance performance.
Xi, also Chinese president and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in a recent instruction, which was studied at a meeting of the CPC Central Leading Group for Party Building held on Monday.
Xi stressed that establishing and putting into practice a correct view of governance performance is a long-term task that requires sustained efforts.
Since the 18th CPC National Congress, the organization of study and education campaigns across the Party to address major and pressing issues in Party building has become an important institutional arrangement, Xi said, lauding the notable results achieved in the latest campaign.
Xi emphasized the need to regularly conduct education on the correct view of governance performance, guiding Party members and officials to always take responsibility, perform their duties and fulfill their obligations in accordance with such a view.
Efforts should also be made to improve differentiated assessment and evaluation systems, and establish a personnel selection and appointment orientation that values solid work and concrete results, Xi said.
During the meeting, participants thoroughly studied and implemented Xi's instruction, reviewed the campaign, and made arrangements for consolidating and expanding the campaign's outcomes and establishing a long-term mechanism accordingly.
The meeting was chaired by Cai Qi, who is head of the CPC Central Leading Group for Party Building, and was also attended by Li Xi, the group's deputy head. Cai and Li, both of whom are members of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, also delivered speeches.
The meeting noted that the campaign has resolved prominent issues related to deviations in view of governance performance, regulated the official conduct of leading officials at all levels, and given a strong boost to all work aimed at ensuring a good start to the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030).
The campaign, which started in late February, has basically concluded and aimed to correct misguided views on governance that often breed vanity projects, hidden risks, heavy burdens on local communities, and public discontent.

item.title: Xi calls on China, Jordan to further deepen alignment of development strategies
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-25
China and Jordan should further deepen the alignment of development strategies, Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Monday.
BEIJING, Aug. 24 (Xinhua) -- China and Jordan should further deepen the alignment of development strategies, Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Monday.
Both sides should enhance cooperation in traditional fields including economy and trade, infrastructure construction, transportation and mining, expand new drivers of cooperation in digital economy, artificial intelligence and green energy, and comprehensively deepen exchanges in education, culture, science and technology, tourism and other areas, Xi said when holding talks with King of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan Abdullah II ibn Al Hussein in Beijing.
Xi noted that in 2015, the two heads of state jointly announced the establishment of China-Jordan strategic partnership, opening a new chapter in the development of bilateral relations.
Facing an international and regional situation characterized by intertwined changes and chaos, building a more substantive and dynamic China-Jordan relationship is in line with the common expectations of the two peoples and also conforms to the general trend of the pursuit of the Global South for strength through unity, he said.
Xi emphasized that China attaches great importance to Jordan's unique and significant role in the region, firmly supports Jordan in safeguarding its national sovereignty, security and development interests, and is willing to maintain close exchanges with Jordan at all levels including the governments, political parties, legislative bodies and localities, and enhance exchanges of experience in governance.
China is willing to work with Jordan to implement the four major global initiatives, enhance coordination and cooperation in multilateral institutions including the United Nations, jointly safeguard the international system with the United Nations at its core and the international order underpinned by international law, and promote the building of a community with a shared future for humanity, Xi said.
King Abdullah II said Jordan and China have established a strong strategic partnership, with fruitful cooperation across various fields. He said Jordan firmly upholds the one-China policy and regards Taiwan as part of China's territory.
Jordan places high priority on its relations with China and is dedicated to expanding cooperation and exchanges in economy and trade, manufacturing, agriculture, science and technology, pharmaceuticals, culture and education, King Abdullah II said, adding that Jordan welcomes more Chinese enterprises to invest there to achieve common development and prosperity.
Jordan speaks highly of the four global initiatives put forward by President Xi and looks forward to China's greater leading role on the global stage, King Abdullah II said.
After the talks, the two heads of state jointly attended a signing ceremony for multiple cooperation documents in areas such as diplomacy, economy and trade, industrial and supply chains, and justice.
The two sides also issued a joint statement on deepening the strategic partnership between China and Jordan.
Prior to the talks in the Great Hall of the People, Xi held a welcome ceremony for King Abdullah II. Xi also hosted a welcome banquet for him in the evening.

item.title: China's wild Asian elephant population nears 400
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-14
Thanks to sustained conservation efforts, China's wild Asian elephant population has more than doubled over the past four decades to nearly 400, according to the latest data from the National Forestry and Grassland Administration (NFGA).
